title.narrative: Reduced incidence of HIV/AIDS infection and improved protection of infected and affected people through non-discriminatory policies

description.narrative: HIV/AIDS remains a significant public health challenge in Ghana, Africa, and globally. The Ghana Aids Commission estimated that the 2023 national adult HIV prevalence in Ghana is estimated at 1.53%, with approximately 334,095 people living with HIV. This includes 316,545 adults (94.7%) and 17,550 children (5.3%). Although, the fight against HIV in Ghana has seen significant progress, but challenges persist, especially concerning disparities among different populations. By implementing targeted strategies, expanding access to HIV care, and investing in public health efforts, Ghana can continue its journey towards an HIV-free generation. The ILO intervention will address the regulatory framework through the revision of the HIV at Workplace Policy to promote voluntary counselling and testing (VCT) as well as self-testing especially with the working population. The policy will also map out startegies to promote healthy living amongst workers and their family members at risk or already infected with HIV.
